title: Training module: attendance and the controlled-agreement attendance allowance
content:
**Prescriptions & Renewals training — attendance when a controlled-substance agreement is signed.**

**The rule.** The attendance allowance combines missed visits and recent care with the prescribing department: where the patient has no missed visit with that department in the last 12 calendar months and a completed in-person visit with it no more than 183 days before the signing day, it allows 30 days; where the patient has exactly one missed visit with that department in those 12 months and a completed in-person visit with it no more than 183 days before, it allows 21 days; otherwise it allows the starting 14 days.

**Questions answered.**

*What is a missed visit?* A visit among the patient's In-Person Appointments with the department of the prescriber on this prescription, recorded as a no-show, scheduled within the 12 calendar months before the signing day. A missed visit with another department does not count.

*What is a completed in-person visit?* An In-Person Appointments visit with that department recorded as completed; the latest one is used, and the days are counted from its date to the signing day. A virtual visit is not an in-person visit.

*Is 183 days itself recent enough?* Yes: "no more than 183 days" includes 183.

**Combinations.**

| Missed visits with the prescribing department in 12 months | Latest completed in-person visit no more than 183 days before | Attendance allowance |
|---|---|---|
| none | yes | 30 days |
| exactly one | yes | 21 days |
| two or more | yes | 14 days |
| any number | no, or no such visit | 14 days |

**Cases (hypothetical).**
- No no-shows with the department and an in-person visit 90 days ago: 30 days.
- One no-show with the department, one no-show with another department, and an in-person visit 120 days ago: only the first counts, so 21 days.
- No no-shows, but the only recent contact was a Virtual Care video visit and the last in-person visit was 200 days ago: 14 days.
